implemented: Element::text_area reuses the controlled TextFieldState/TextEdit, ScrollSpec and clipboard contracts; canonical text, selection, scroll and byte policy remain client-owned.
One source-indexed grapheme row map drives wrapping, hit testing, selection, caret, visual navigation and bounded visible-row painting.
Pending GPU frames do not defer client updates or fresh CPU input geometry; unrelated wallpaper redraws do not rewrap idle Notes.
Notes fills its actual resized bounds and saves accepted content only through the existing root persistence coordinator.
Single-line, masked and multiline placeholder opacity comes from the shared design recipe and semantic token.

cpu_measurement.contention: Existing video-wallpaper VM remained running; no isolated-host claim.
cpu_measurement.timing_scope: Optimized host CPU-only UI layout/edit/navigation at an 8192-byte client bound; one CPU quota; existing video VM remains running. No GPU/native delivery or end-to-end latency claim.

visual_acceptance.scope: Software-Vulkan fixture comparisons in both themes at 1x/2x, including multiline and resized Notes. This is separate from native caret/selection pixel acceptance.

native_acceptance.scope: Native single-output ordinary Notes editing on the prepared software-Vulkan VM; no hardware GPU or performance claim.

history.cause: The restoration guard required the inactive unit label. Orderly child termination left the old supervisor unit failed with exit status 241, although it was quiescent; the guard correctly refused to restore settings without its required stop proof.
history.correction: The harness now captures the exact unit cgroup before stopping and requires no desktop process, zero main/control PIDs and an absent or recursively empty cgroup before restoring owned settings. A quiescent failed unit is admitted; a live process is not.

not_covered: native scrollbar thumb and rendered caret/selection clipping
native soft-wrap affinity and exact scroll-offset assertions
native PageUp/PageDown and stationary edge-drag autoscroll
GTK, Chrome or other third-party GUI application clipboard interoperability

limits: One optimized host run with a one-CPU quota and a running video VM. These observations are not timing thresholds, a statistically repeatable result or a before/after CPU improvement.
Layout/edit/navigation timings cover CPU view/layout/input synchronization and current-model updates/reveal; they exclude GPU, native input delivery, count/geometry assertions and scene teardown.
Visible-row painting is bounded, but layout still measures the full client-owned document. This is an 8192-byte Notes editor, not virtualized large-document layout.
No current desktop RSS, GPU completion, scanout, end-to-end input latency or native 60 FPS result is established by this measurement.

Complex-script shaping, bidirectional layout, font fallback, preedit/IME and third-party GUI application clipboard interoperability remain separate requirements. Accessibility remains deferred by the user.
There is no stationary-pointer selection autoscroll timer. Selection reveal remains input-driven.

Native pixel-level caret/selection clipping, scrollbar thumb dragging, soft-wrap affinity, exact scroll offsets, PageUp/PageDown and delayed clipboard/focus-retirement races remain unverified by this run.

supervisor_follow_up.scope: The committed supervisor script and one owned KillMode=mixed user drop-in were upgraded separately in the existing VM. Two 35-second stable starts and an intervening clean exit-0 stop passed while retaining the accepted Notes UI binary. Settings, wallpaper/source/theme and the initially empty clipboard/history were verified without rewriting them. This does not broaden Notes native coverage or establish crash/device-loss recovery.
